To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the suppressor of the cytokine signal 3 (SOCSI3) is up‐regulated and the suppressor of signal transducer and activators of transcription‐3/interleukin‐17 pathway in Sjögrens syndrome.
SOCS3 is up‐regulated but functionally impaired in SS.
the expression of SOCS-3 in peripheral blood monocytes and salivary glands is significantly increased in Sjogren's syndrome compared to healthy controls.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the suppressor cytokine‐signalling 3 (SOSS3) in the pathogenesis of Sjogren's syndrome.
the role of SOCS3 and its interaction with STAT‐3 in the regulation of IL‐17, which is a key factor driving the autoimmune process in SS.
the regulation of IL‐17 by SOCS3 and the role of the JAK/STAT‐3/SOCS3 pathway in the development of SS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is dysregulation of SOCS3 signalling in SS.
there are increased levels of SOCS-3 in the peripheral blood mononucleocytes and salivary glands from Sjögren’s syndrome (SS) patients, but that this is not sufficient to regulate IL-17 expression.
the SOCS3‐STAT‐3‐IL‐17 pathway in Sjögrens Syndrome is dysregulated, with the result that the expression of the inflammatory cytokine IL‐7 is not appropriately downregulated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the suppressor of SOCS3‐STAT‐3‐IL‐17 pathway is dysregulated in Sjögrens syndrome.
SOCS3 is up‐regulated, but its negative regulatory role is lost.
SOCS3 is up‐regulated, but is unable to suppress IL‐17 in the pathogenesis of Sjörgen's syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SOCS3–JAK/STAT‐3 pathway is dysregulated in SS.
the dysregulation of SOCS3‐STAT‐3 signalling in SS is a result of a reduction in the functional capacity of SOCS3, which in turn leads to an unregulated IL‐17 production.
the dysregulated expression of the suppressor cytokine‐signalling 3 (SOCCS3) in patients with Sjogren's syndrome (pSS) may be a key factor in the pathophysiology of this condition.
